Inside the square there are several horizontal and vertical broken line segments, and these line segments are arranged symmetrically with respect to diagonal AC; the gray shaded part and the white unshaded part form a mirror-image complementary relationship on the two sides of diagonal AC. The problem gives the side length of the square as 2 cm and asks for the area of the shaded part. Reasoning: After the square is reflected along diagonal AC, it still coincides with itself, and reflection preserves area. From the symmetry relationship in the figure, it can be known that the shaded region, after being reflected with respect to AC, exactly corresponds to the unshaded region, so the shaded area equals the unshaded area. Therefore the shaded area is half of the area of the whole square. The area of the square is 2 × 2 = 4 cm², so the shaded area is 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm².

Since reflecting the shaded region across AC gives exactly the unshaded region, the shaded and unshaded areas are equal. Therefore the shaded area is half the square area: (1/2)·2^2 = 2 cm^2.
